title: Merge Intervals
description:
Given an unordered list of closed integer intervals [start, end], combine intervals that share at least one point. Return the smallest collection of closed intervals covering exactly the same points. If the input is empty, return an empty list. A single input interval must remain present, including one with equal start and end.

Sort ranges by start and then end, and grow the right endpoint of the most recently emitted range whenever the next start is at most that endpoint. Once a new start is strictly larger than the current end, no subsequent sorted range can bridge the gap back to this component, so it is safe to emit a new interval. Endpoint contact counts as overlap, but a one-integer gap does not.

The result must be sorted by ascending start, with ascending end as the tie-breaker, and contain maximal nonoverlapping intervals. Do not return the intervals in their original shuffled order or mutate the supplied pairs. For instance, [1,4] and [4,5] become [1,5].

Example 1:

Input: intervals = [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]
Output: [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]

Example 2:

Input: intervals = [[1,4],[4,5]]
Output: [[1,5]]

Example 3:

Input: intervals = []
Output: []

Constraints:

  • 0 <= intervals.length <= 100,000
  • -1,000,000 <= start <= end <= 1,000,000
  • Each interval contains two integer endpoints.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Only the first two ranges overlap.
There are no ranges to combine.
